issues.description: In solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java the private fields are declared using snake_case identifiers (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) but the constructor parameters and all accessor/mutator methods use camelCase identifiers (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) and assign/read those camelCase names. The UML in the problem statement (problem_statement.md lines 63-69) also specifies camelCase attribute names. This mismatch means the constructor and methods in the solution refer to field names that are not declared, which will cause compilation errors and will confuse students mapping the UML to the implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make field names consistent across artifacts. Rename the private fields in solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java to the camelCase names used in the constructor and methods (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors) to match the UML and the rest of the implementation. Alternatively, change all constructor parameter and method references to the declared snake_case names, but prefer aligning to the UML/camelCase to follow Java conventions and avoid confusing students.
